organizations.normalization_notes: The NARA-published chapter uses Service de Renseignement or SR for the French intelligence organization in Algiers. This historical service is not silently merged with a later French intelligence agency.
Naval Reserve service and OSS attachment are modeled as a military pathway, not civilian employment.

affiliations.organization_name_as_found: French intelligence (Service de Renseignement, or SR)
affiliations.date_precision: The NARA-published chapter identifies Colonel Chretien among French SR officers with whom the OSS quickly cooperated after establishing its Algiers headquarters; it gives no formal transfer date or personnel status.
affiliations.research_notes: The exact name, colonel rank, French nationality note and direct OSS cooperation align. The evidence documents a French military-intelligence pathway and cooperation, not that Chretien became an OSS employee or held a civilian job.

affiliations.date_precision: Notre Dame's contemporary volume places John L. Chrislow in the class commissioned as USNR ensigns on 27 May 1943. NARA later lists John Laurence Chrislow in OSS Naval Officers Personnel Cards, but the exact OSS assignment date is absent.
affiliations.research_notes: The uncommon exact name, NARA-expanded middle name, Naval Officers card series and contemporary USNR commissioning roster form a strong bridge. No source yet supplies a direct school-to-OSS transfer order or a civilian employer.

claims.claim_text: The indexed French Colonel Jean Chretien is a high-confidence match to the Colonel Jean Chretien documented in NARA's history of OSS cooperation with French intelligence in Algiers.
claims.evidence_excerpt: The OSS quickly cooperated with Col. Louis Rivet, Col. Jean Chretien
claims.evidence_paraphrase: A NARA-published chapter names Colonel Jean Chretien among French intelligence officers with whom OSS cooperated in Algiers.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The exact name, colonel rank, French nationality and direct OSS relationship align across the index and a NARA-published operational history; Box 122 has not been reviewed.
claims.temporal_assessment: The chapter places the relationship after OSS established its Algiers headquarters following the November 1942 North Africa landings.
claims.match_notes: The project publishes the identity at high confidence while preserving the index spelling without an accent and not adding unsupported full given names.

claims.claim_text: The best-supported immediate pathway for John Laurence Chrislow is his 1943 commissioning as a U.S. Naval Reserve ensign before documented service in the OSS Naval Officers record series.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Today, May 27, 1943 more than 1000 midshipmen are being commissioned Ensigns USNR.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Notre Dame's contemporary class volume lists John L. Chrislow in the class commissioned as USNR ensigns; NARA later places his full name in OSS Naval Officers cards.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence identity from the uncommon exact name, NARA-expanded middle name, naval record type, hometown and education.
claims.temporal_assessment: Probable immediate military pathway. The sources establish a May 1943 commission and later OSS naval-officer documentation but not the exact assignment or transfer date.
claims.match_notes: Published as a qualified military assignment. University attendance is preserved as identity evidence and is not classified as employment.

claims.claim_text: A 1946 Shanghai intelligence cable naming Anthony M. Chrisler is a possible but unconfirmed identity lead for the indexed person.
claims.evidence_excerpt: CHARLES R. ETHRIDGE, KEITH W. CORNELL AND ANTHONY M. CHRISLER
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The cable appoints an exact-name Anthony M. Chrisler as a CAP-5 radio operator in Shanghai in August 1946.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The exact full name and immediate postwar intelligence context are relevant, but no Box 122, service, hometown, birth or wartime OSS identifier connects the records.
claims.temporal_assessment: The source is postwar and does not establish pre-OSS employment, military service or an OSS start date.
claims.match_notes: Retained for human review only. It is excluded from public facts and default analytics.

person_updates.identity_evidence: The visually verified index row supplies Jean Chretien, Colonel, marked French, Box 122. A NARA-published operational history independently names Colonel Jean Chretien among French intelligence officers with whom OSS cooperated in Algiers. Exact name, rank, nationality and direct OSS context align; the physical file remains unreviewed.
person_updates.next_action: Review Box 122 and the relevant French military file to confirm full identity, unit, exact SR position, formal relationship to OSS and any civilian employment before career military service.

research_attempts.query_text: NARA OSS index page 80 context; exact-name, accented-name, colonel, French intelligence and OSS searches; NARA publication body and provenance review; CIA, institutional, military-file, obituary, newspaper and archival checks for Jean Chretien.
research_attempts.rejection_reasons: Unsourced biography mirrors and discovery-only pages were not accepted; the uninspected French military-file reference remains a lead rather than evidence; no civilian employer claim was inferred.
research_attempts.research_notes: The NARA-published operational history supports a high-confidence identity and qualified French SR military pathway. It documents cooperation rather than a formal OSS transfer. No full identifier, raw Catalog response or copyrighted page is retained.
research_attempts.next_action: Review Box 122 and the relevant French military file to confirm full identity, unit, exact SR position, formal relationship to OSS and any civilian employment before career military service.
